title: Installing and updating
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.

title: Choose your download
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Open the Downloads page . Choose your operating system and processor. Use arm64 for Apple Silicon and most recent Android phones; x64 is for Intel or AMD desktop processors. If you are unsure on Android, choose the universal APK. Use a regular release for everyday use. Development and nightly builds may contain unfinished changes. The Downloads page lists current requirements and package-manager commands. OpenTubeX supports Windows, macOS, Linux, and an Android app . An experimental iOS/iPadOS app is available for version 17.4 and newer.

title: Windows
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Download the Windows installer matching your processor, or follow the winget instructions . Open the installer and complete its prompts. Launch OpenTubeX from the Start menu. For a portable download, extract the archive before launching the application. Keep the extracted files together.

title: macOS
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Download the DMG for Apple Silicon (arm64) or Intel (x64) . Open it and drag OpenTubeX into Applications . Open OpenTubeX from Applications. OpenTubeX is not notarized by Apple. If the first launch is blocked, allow the app in System Settings → Privacy & Security after checking that you downloaded it from the official release. Homebrew users can follow the Homebrew instructions .

title: Linux
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Choose a package matching your distribution on the Downloads page . Follow the linked repository instructions, or open a downloaded DEB/RPM with your distribution’s package installer. Launch OpenTubeX from your application menu. For an AppImage, open the file’s properties, allow it to run as a program, then launch it. For a portable archive, extract it first and run the included OpenTubeX executable. Repository installations are convenient when you want updates through your normal package manager.

title: Android
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: On the Downloads page , choose F-Droid or Obtainium . For a manual installation, download an APK from GitHub Releases . Pick the regular APK unless you want OpenTubeX Lite . Follow the selected installer’s prompts. For a direct APK, Android may ask you to allow installation from the browser or file manager you used. Open the app. Allow notifications if you want download progress and playback controls in Android’s notification area. The Android app has a phone layout, background playback, and offline downloads. Desktop integrations and window controls can differ or be unavailable.

title: OpenTubeX Lite
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Releases also include smaller Lite APKs. Lite leaves out yt-dlp, so it has no downloads, no yt-dlp stream extraction, no playback of links from other sites, and no yt-dlp cookies. It installs as a separate app, org.opentubex.app.lite , with its own settings and library, so you can install both. To move your data between them, export your library in one and import it in the other.

title: iOS / iPadOS (experimental)
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.

title: SideStore: refresh without a computer
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: We recommend SideStore for regular use because refreshes can run on your device after initial computer setup. OpenTubeX installation has been tested with iloader; the SideStore recommendation is based on its documented refresh workflow. Follow SideStore’s prerequisites and installation guide . The guide uses iloader on your computer for initial installation and sets up the required pairing file and local VPN. Trust your Apple Account under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management . Enable Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode , restart, and confirm when prompted. Connect the local VPN required by SideStore, open SideStore, and complete its initial refresh. Open the official OpenTubeX SideStore source on your device and tap Add to SideStore . Alternatively, paste https://sidestore.opentubex.org/source.json into Browse → Sources → + . Choose OpenTubeX for stable beta releases or OpenTubeX Nightly for development builds, then install it. You can also import a downloaded IPA from My Apps using the + button. With a free Apple Account, refresh both SideStore and OpenTubeX within seven days . Check their expiry counters; background refresh is not a guarantee. Keep SideStore’s required local VPN available when refreshing. SideStore does not remove Apple’s expiry requirement. If SideStore itself expires, reinstall it from your computer. You may also need the computer to replace an expired pairing file, for example after an OS update or reset. See SideStore troubleshooting .

title: Manual IPA installation
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Download the unsigned .ipa from the iOS / iPadOS download card . One IPA supports both iPhone and iPad. Opening it in Files does not install it: a sideloading tool must sign it with your Apple Account first.

title: iloader: tested computer installation
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: iloader has been used to install and update OpenTubeX on a physical iPad. It runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install iloader from its official website or GitHub releases and follow its platform prerequisites. Connect your iPhone or iPad over USB, unlock it, and trust the computer. In iloader, sign in with your Apple Account, select your device, and import the OpenTubeX IPA. Trust your developer account and enable Developer Mode as described above, then open OpenTubeX. With a free account, reconnect to your computer and install the IPA again before its seven-day signature expires.

title: Other signing options and limits
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: AltStore Classic can also install IPAs, but refreshing still needs a computer running AltServer over Wi-Fi or USB. AltStore PAL cannot install arbitrary IPA files and is not an installation option for this build. Free Apple Accounts allow three active sideloaded apps, including SideStore or AltStore itself. OpenTubeX and OpenTubeX Nightly install as separate apps with independent settings and libraries; keeping both alongside SideStore uses all three slots. A paid Apple Developer membership provides longer signing periods; it is optional. For updates, use the update offered by the OpenTubeX source in SideStore, or import the newer IPA with the same signing tool and Apple Account over the existing app. Avoid uninstalling it: that removes its local data. Older nightly IPAs shared the stable app’s identity; installing the new separate nightly app does not transfer that library. Export your library before switching channels, signing tools, or accounts. Refreshing renews the signature; it does not necessarily update OpenTubeX to a newer release.

title: Current iOS limitations
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: The port is experimental. Playback, fullscreen, touch menus, and settings have been tested on a physical iPad, but broader device coverage is still in progress. Authenticated playback, translated audio, app-managed proxies, alternate icons, and closed-app subscription refresh are unavailable on iOS. Track progress in the iOS port issue .

title: Update without starting over
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Export your data before changing release channels or reinstalling. If you installed through a package manager, F-Droid, or Obtainium, use that same tool to update. For a manual installation, get the newer package for the same platform and install it over the existing app. For a portable installation, keep your existing data when replacing the app files. Reopen the app and check your subscriptions and playlists. Settings → General → Check for Updates controls whether OpenTubeX tells you about new releases; it does not replace your package manager’s update process. See the Changelog for release changes. Avoid uninstalling or clearing application data just to update.

title: Subscriptions and playlists
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.

title: Find a video or channel
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Enter a title, channel name, or YouTube link in the search field. Submit the search and open a result. Open the channel name to browse more uploads from that creator. OpenTubeX keeps your subscriptions and local playlists in the app. You do not need to sign in to YouTube, and these changes do not update your YouTube account.

title: Subscribe to a channel
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Open the channel you want to follow. Select Subscribe . Open Subscriptions in the navigation to see uploads from your channels. On a small screen, some navigation entries are under More . Use the feed’s refresh action to fetch new uploads. Already have subscriptions elsewhere? Import your existing subscriptions instead of adding channels one by one.

title: Use profiles
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Profiles let you group channels, for example into work and leisure viewing. Open the profile menu from your profile icon. Use the profile selector to choose or manage a profile. Check which profile is active when viewing your subscriptions. If a channel appears to be missing, check All Channels before importing it again. Feed filters can also hide videos, Shorts, or live content. To filter a feed without switching profiles, create a subscription group with New Group on the Channels page. For step-by-step profile creation, groups, and bulk channel management, see Organize channels with profiles .

title: Create a local playlist
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Open Playlists in the navigation. Select Create New Playlist . Enter a name and select Create . On a video, use Add to Playlist and choose the playlist. On desktop, video cards also expose actions on hover; use the video’s menu when an action is not visible. Return to Playlists and open your playlist to watch its videos. New Playlist Name dialog with an example name and Create and Cancel buttons. Give the playlist a name, then select Create. This example uses “Watch this weekend”. Local playlists are stored by OpenTubeX. They are separate from public YouTube playlists, and adding a video does not download it. See Downloads to save media for offline use.

title: Open settings
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Select your profile icon to open the quick settings menu. Choose All settings . Select a category or use settings search to find an option by name. OpenTubeX quick settings menu with the All settings gear in the upper-right corner. Select the gear at the top right of quick settings to open All settings. Start with Playback and settings for captions, autoplay, appearance, and SponsorBlock. Back up your library once you have it set up.

title: Organize channels with profiles
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Profiles group your subscribed channels into separate feeds, such as music, learning, or news. They are channel groups within the app, not separate Google accounts. For a lighter way to filter one feed, use subscription groups instead. Profiles switch the whole app to a different set of channels; groups filter the feed of the current profile.

title: Create a profile
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Data . Select Manage Subscriptions to open the profile manager. Choose Create New Profile . Enter a name, choose its appearance, then select Create Profile . Profile Manager showing the color picker, a Learning profile name, profile preview, and Create Profile button. Choose a color and name, check the profile preview, then select Create Profile. The default All Channels profile collects your subscriptions. Use an additional profile when you want to focus on a subset.

title: Switch the feed you see
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Open the profile menu from the profile icon. Choose a profile in the profile selector. Open Subscriptions to view that profile’s channels. An empty profile has no channels to show. Switching profiles is not a way to create separate watch-history or playlist libraries.

title: Add channels
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: To add a new channel, switch to your desired profile, open the channel, and select Subscribe . The channel is also included in All Channels . Once you have more than one profile, the arrow next to Subscribe opens Subscription settings , where you can tick the profiles and groups the channel belongs to without switching profiles. To organize channels you already follow: Open Manage Subscriptions , choose the profile you want to edit, and open the Manage profile subscriptions tab. Select channels from the available channel list. Choose Add Selected To Profile . Return to your subscription feed and check the active profile.

title: Remove channels carefully
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Switch to a profile and use Unsubscribe on a channel to remove it from that group. The profile manager also offers bulk selection for managing channels. Removing a channel from All Channels removes it from the other profiles too. If you only want it out of one group, edit that group instead. Export your subscriptions before reorganizing a large library.

title: Use subscription groups
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Groups are filters inside a profile, such as Music or Gaming. A channel can be in several groups. Open Channels and select New Group . Enter a Group Name , choose its channels, and select Create . In Subscriptions or Channels , select a group chip to show only its channels; select All to show everything again. Once a group exists, the New Group and Edit Group buttons appear next to the chips on both pages. Use Edit Group to change or delete the selected group. Deleting a group keeps its channels subscribed. You can also add a channel to a group from its Subscription settings .

title: Back up profiles
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Use Settings → Data & Storage → Data → Export Subscriptions → Export OpenTubeX . That format preserves profile information for importing on another OpenTubeX installation. Subscription groups and the custom channel order are settings, so the subscriptions export leaves them out. Use Export Settings , or Export backup with the settings category selected, to keep them. See Back up your library .

title: Importing and backing up data
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.

title: Find the import and export controls
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Open your profile menu and select All settings . Select Data & Storage . Open the Data tab. Choose Export backup or Import backup for one OpenTubeX ZIP, an action for an individual file, or Import YouTube Takeout ZIP for a downloaded YouTube archive. Data settings with unified backup controls, a YouTube Takeout ZIP import button, and individual import and export actions. Desktop Data settings. Import a YouTube Takeout ZIP directly, or choose an action for an individual file.

title: Import subscriptions
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Export subscriptions from your previous app. For YouTube, request a YouTube data export through Google Takeout , including subscriptions. Select Import Subscriptions and choose the individual file. For Takeout, extract subscriptions/subscriptions.csv from the ZIP first, or use Import YouTube Takeout ZIP to select the archive, choose the categories to import, select Preview changes , then Import selected data . Wait for the import result. Open Subscriptions , check the active profile, and refresh the feed. Supported subscription formats include OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db , YouTube Takeout .csv , .json , or .opml , NewPipe .json , and LibreTube backup or FreeTube export .json . A JSON file must contain the expected export data; renaming a different file does not convert it.

title: Get your subscriptions from YouTube
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Follow the Google Takeout walkthrough to export subscriptions, history, and playlists. It covers export selection, the JSON history format, and importing the ZIP directly.

title: Move from another app
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Export a subscription file from your previous app, then transfer it to the device running OpenTubeX. Use a subscriptions export rather than a full archive when your app offers both. For OpenTubeX or FreeTube, keep the original .db file; for NewPipe, use its subscriptions .json export. Import the file with the steps above. The client comparison lists the FreeTube data that OpenTubeX can import.

title: Import history or playlists
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: In the Data tab, choose Import History , Import Playlists , or Import search history . Select the matching exported file and wait for the result. Open the corresponding library page to check the imported entries. History accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db, YouTube Takeout .json, and LibreTube backup .json. Search history accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db and YouTube Takeout .json. Import Playlists accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db exports and individual YouTube Takeout playlist .csv files. Use Import YouTube Takeout ZIP for multiple Takeout playlists together. If imported history has missing details or incorrect LIVE labels, use Repair History .

title: Back up your library
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Data and select Export backup . Choose the categories to include, select Export selected data , then save the ZIP file in a backup location you can find on your other device. On that device, select Import backup and choose the ZIP. OpenTubeX offers only the categories the ZIP contains and previews how many items are new, already present, or skipped. Select the categories to import, then Import selected data . The ZIP contains separate JSON files for the selected categories: profiles and subscriptions, playlists, watch history, search history, watch statistics, and transferable settings. All categories are selected by default. Importing merges the selected categories with data already on the device; records with matching IDs or dates are updated. You can still export or import individual categories using the separate actions. The ZIP does not include open tab sessions or the entire application profile. Transferable settings omit device-specific options and sync credentials, such as proxy configuration, external-player paths, screenshot folders, and the sync privacy key. Configure sync separately on the other device using the sync setup guide .

title: Back up on a schedule
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: On desktop, Scheduled backups in Settings → Data & Storage → Data saves a complete backup ZIP to a folder you choose. Select Choose backup folder , turn on Enable scheduled backups , and pick a Backup frequency of daily, weekly, or every 30 days, and how many backups to keep. Backups run while OpenTubeX is open; a missed backup runs at the next startup. Exports contain your personal viewing data; store them privately. For a full desktop profile backup, follow Back up or move to another device . Downloaded video and audio files are separate from these exports and the profile backup; copy those files separately if you need them.

title: If an import fails
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Check the file type against the supported formats above and make sure you selected the correct action. For YouTube Takeout ZIPs, check that the archive contains the selected data and that history was exported as JSON. Keep the original export unchanged. If an import reports skipped items, inspect the result before assuming everything transferred. See Troubleshooting for the next steps.

title: Import from Google Takeout
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Google Takeout exports your Google account data. OpenTubeX can import subscriptions, watch history, search history, and playlists directly from the ZIP; you do not need to sign in to Google inside OpenTubeX.

title: Choose your YouTube data
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Open Google Takeout in your browser and sign in to the account you use for YouTube. The link shows Takeout in English to match the steps below. OpenTubeX can import an export in any language. Choose Deselect all , then select YouTube and YouTube Music . Open All YouTube data included . Deselect everything in that dialog, then select subscriptions , history , and/or playlists for the data you want. Confirm with OK . Selecting only these categories keeps the export smaller. If you use more than one Google account, check which account is selected before exporting. Google Takeout content-options dialog with history selected. Select history for watch and search history. You can also select subscriptions and playlists. The screenshots show the relevant controls, but are not captures of today’s interface. Google may change the layout and labels.

title: Choose JSON for history
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: In the YouTube and YouTube Music entry, open Multiple formats . Change History to JSON and confirm with OK . Select Next step . Google Takeout format dialog with history set to JSON. Set history to JSON before requesting the export. Google Takeout YouTube entry showing JSON format, one data type selected, and the Next step button. After making your choices, the buttons may read JSON format and a count of selected types rather than Multiple formats and All YouTube data included. This example includes history only. This step matters for watch and search history. OpenTubeX expects a JSON history export, not Takeout’s HTML version. Subscription exports use CSV. Renaming an HTML file to .json does not convert it.

title: Create and download the export
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Choose Send download link via email , Export once , and .zip . Select Create export . Wait for Google to prepare the archive. Use the download link when it is ready; Google may ask you to sign in again. Download the ZIP. If Google splits the export into several archives, import each ZIP that contains YouTube data. You do not need to upload the archive to another website. Creating an export does not delete your data from Google. Google’s export help covers delivery options and account-specific problems.

title: Import the ZIP
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: In OpenTubeX, open your profile menu, choose All settings , then Data & Storage → Data . Choose Import YouTube Takeout ZIP and select the downloaded ZIP. OpenTubeX detects subscriptions, watch history, search history, and playlists in the archive. Uncheck anything you do not want to import, then choose Preview changes to see how many items are new, already present, or skipped. Choose Import selected data . Check the corresponding library pages. Refresh the subscription feed to fetch channel uploads. Takeout ZIP import screen with checkboxes for detected subscriptions, history, search history, and playlists, a preview of new and existing items for each, and the Import selected data button. OpenTubeX Data settings showing Import YouTube Takeout ZIP and separate data import actions. Choose Import YouTube Takeout ZIP to select the archive directly.

title: Import individual files
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Extract the downloaded ZIP and open Takeout/YouTube and YouTube Music/ . Exports in other languages use translated folder and file names, so select the translated equivalents of the paths in step 3. In OpenTubeX, open Settings → Data & Storage → Data . Choose Import Subscriptions for subscriptions/subscriptions.csv , Import History for history/watch-history.json , or Import search history for history/search-history.json . Check the imported data and refresh the subscription feed. For a Takeout playlist CSV, choose Import Playlists and select an individual file in playlists/ , or use ZIP import for several playlists together.

title: If something is missing
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Only HTML history files: create another export with History set to JSON. No supported YouTube data found: check the account and the selected data categories. The ZIP importer recognizes YouTube data by its contents, so translated folder and file names do not affect it. The archive’s archive_browser.html is an index, not importable data. Older history is missing: the export can only contain data Google still retains. Previously deleted activity may not be recoverable. Imported history has missing details or incorrect LIVE labels: use Repair History to fetch the available details without changing watched status or progress. A channel is missing after import: check the import result and your active profile . A removed channel or incomplete export may need investigation. A playlist video shows only its ID: Takeout’s playlist CSV includes video IDs and timestamps, but no video titles or durations. Select Repair Playlists on the Playlists page to fetch the missing details without changing the playlist order. Keep your original archive until you have checked the imported data. See Importing and backing up data for other supported formats.

title: Sources and image credits
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Takeout instructions are adapted from FreeTube’s subscription and history guides ( MIT license ), with OpenTubeX-specific import steps. General export behavior is checked against Google Account Help . The three Google Takeout UI screenshots are reproduced unchanged from positron48’s source images , published with Positroid’s September 2025 walkthrough . Google product visuals belong to Google and are shown for instructional purposes. See Google’s educational-use guidance . OpenTubeX is not affiliated with Google.

title: Sync between devices
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: Sync shares selected library data between your OpenTubeX installations. Export your library before connecting devices or changing your setup. Sync can propagate changes and deletions; keep a separate backup. See the device sync comparison .

title: Choose a server
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: The default public OpenTubeX sync server supports all sync features with end-to-end encryption. The app encrypts synced data on your device before uploading it; only your devices hold the key. The server still receives account and connection metadata. You can also use a self-hosted OpenTubeX server. LibreTube sync servers are supported, but do not support end-to-end encryption or certain sync features. Read the Privacy policy for this server link when available. The network exposure table explains what a sync operator can observe.

title: Connect your first device
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: Open Settings → Sync and turn on Enable Sync . Enter or select the Sync server URL and wait for the server check. Enter your Username and account Password . For encrypted sync, also enter a separate Privacy passphrase . Use the same privacy passphrase when signing in to an existing encrypted account. Choose Register to create an account if the server allows registration, or Log in for an existing account. Check the connection and privacy status, then review the categories described below. Use Sync now and wait for synchronization to finish before pairing another device. Sync settings with Enable Sync, Sync server URL, Username, Password, and a separate Privacy passphrase field. Connect in Settings → Sync. The server address shown is an example, not a public sync service. Keep the privacy passphrase somewhere private that you can recover independently of the app. Your account password authenticates you to the server; the privacy passphrase unlocks encrypted data. Changing the account password does not recover a lost privacy passphrase. If you lose the passphrase and no connected device retains the privacy key, the encrypted data cannot be recovered from the server.

title: Choose what to sync
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: In Settings → Sync , review Subscriptions , Playlists , History , Upcoming reminders , Profiles , Open tabs and session , and Settings . Settings sync does not transfer every device-specific preference or credential. To keep one setting different on this device, select the link icon next to it, labeled Stop syncing this setting . Select it again to resume syncing that setting. Each device keeps its own open tab set by default, including devices of the same type. Enabling Use one shared tab set across devices makes the current device’s tabs the shared set. Other devices replace their open tabs with that set when they sync; tabs from different devices are not combined. Watch stats sync is enabled by default; turn it off to keep statistics on the device. It is separate from the History toggle. Sync settings for an example account with enhanced privacy enabled and separate library, Watch stats, and shared-tab controls. Choose categories separately. This example account keeps automatic sync and shared tabs off. Use Sync now for a manual sync, or enable Sync automatically . If the app stops synchronization to prevent data loss, review the proposed deletions before allowing it to continue.

title: Pair another device
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: Secure pairing transfers the encryption key from a device already connected to your sync account. On the new device, open Settings → Sync , enable sync, and select the same Sync server URL as the connected device. Choose Pair with an existing device , enter a recognizable Device name , and choose Create pairing code . On the already connected device, choose Pair another device and scan the new device’s QR code. Alternatively, choose Use text code instead on the new device and Enter code manually on the connected device, then paste the code and choose Check code . On the connected device, check the request and choose Approve pairing . Compare the verification codes on both devices. On the new device, choose Codes match only if they match. Wait for pairing and sync to finish, then review the new device’s sync categories and library. Pair with an existing device dialog with Living room laptop entered as the device name and a Create pairing code button. Start on the new device: give it a recognizable name, then create its pairing code. If the connected device cannot scan a code, for example because it has no camera, start from the connected device instead. Choose Pair another device , then Show pairing code . On the new device, choose Pair with an existing device and Use code from connected device , and scan or paste that code. Then approve the request on the connected device as in step 4; pairing finishes on its own. Pairing transfers account access and the privacy key without typing your account password or privacy passphrase on the new device. Show the pairing code only to your trusted device. It expires after two minutes; create a new code if it expires, and clear text codes from clipboard history afterward. You can also sign in on the second device with the same server, username, account password, and privacy passphrase. If pairing reports that it cannot verify the key, sync the existing device first and retry.

title: Use sync across devices
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: OpenTubeX sync servers also offer these features; LibreTube servers do not. Account activity in Settings → Sync lists recent changes from your devices, such as a changed setting or a video added to a playlist. To continue a video elsewhere, choose Open on another device in its menu. Offline devices receive it when they reconnect, for up to 24 hours.

title: Manage devices and your password
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: On servers with enhanced privacy, Settings → Sync → Devices lists every device with access to your account, with when it was last active. Use Rename device to change a name, or Revoke access to sign a lost or retired device out. Revoking a device also deletes its synced tab sets. Change password changes your account password and signs out every other device; the current device stays connected. Sign the other devices in again or pair them . This does not change your privacy passphrase.

title: Disconnect or remove the account
description: Connect a sync server, pair another device, and choose what to synchronize.
text: Use Disconnect to disconnect this installation. Delete sync account permanently removes the server account and its stored data, while leaving the current device’s local OpenTubeX data in place. It asks for your account password. Read the confirmation and keep your exports before deleting the account.

title: Playback and settings
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.

title: Use the player
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Open a video. Move the pointer over the player, or tap it on a phone, to reveal controls. Use play/pause, the seek bar, and volume to control playback. Open the player’s settings menu to change quality or playback speed. Available qualities depend on the video and playback engine. Use the captions control to select a subtitle track when one is available. Use fullscreen for a larger view. On desktop, Picture-in-Picture keeps a floating player visible while you work elsewhere. Some controls move into the player’s overflow menu when space is limited. Built-in playback does not support seeking in live streams or premieres. To rewind, choose yt-dlp as the stream extraction method ; seeking is available when YouTube provides a rewindable stream, and the available window may not cover the full broadcast.

title: Play a link from another site
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Paste the full media page URL into OpenTubeX’s search field and submit it. OpenTubeX uses yt-dlp to extract the media. On desktop, allow any required managed tool download to finish; tool settings are under Settings → Advanced → External Software . Use the player controls as usual. Details, chapters, captions, and formats depend on what the source provides. Support depends on yt-dlp and the site; some links require authentication or are unavailable, and DRM-protected media is unsupported. Playing links from other sites needs yt-dlp, so it does not work in OpenTubeX Lite or the web demo. The same applies to seeking in live streams. Opening a link contacts that site and its media services. See Downloads to save supported media offline.

title: Set your playback defaults
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Open Settings → Playback . Adjust default quality, playback rate, or autoplay options to suit your connection and viewing preferences. Set your preferred caption language and appearance if you use subtitles. Open another video to check your defaults. Playback settings showing subtitle, autoplay, volume, and Picture-in-Picture preferences. Desktop Playback settings. Player controls change the current video; settings let you choose defaults. Start Videos Automatically , Autoplay Recommended Videos , and Autoplay Playlist Videos control different behaviors. Turn off the ones you do not want. Per-channel settings can override global preferences, so check those if one channel behaves differently.

title: Find and customize keyboard shortcuts
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: On desktop, open Keyboard Shortcuts from the profile menu to see the current bindings. Select a shortcut and press a new combination to change it. This is also the place to check the bindings for play/pause, seeking, captions, fullscreen, and Picture-in-Picture. Shortcuts can be customized, so the displayed bindings are the source of truth. When typing in search or another text field, move focus back to the player before using playback keys.

title: Choose appearance and content settings
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Appearance: choose a theme and adjust layout and thumbnails. Subscriptions: adjust feed refresh and display options. Add-ons: configure SponsorBlock and other optional services. Choose which SponsorBlock categories should be skipped automatically. Privacy: review viewing privacy options. Data & Storage: import or export your library and inspect storage usage. Sync: connect and pair your devices , end-to-end encrypted on servers with enhanced privacy. Keep the privacy passphrase private and make a backup before changing your setup. See the SponsorBlock guide for skip behaviors and Privacy and watch history for recording controls. Use settings search when you know an option’s name but not its category. The Features page explains additional options such as transcripts and per-channel playback settings.

title: Mobile and Linux differences
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: On Android and iOS/iPadOS, tap to show player controls. Background playback can continue when you switch apps. To keep playing after the screen locks, leave Settings → Playback → Continue playback when the screen is locked on; turn it off to pause when the app is no longer visible. Android’s media notification provides playback controls; on iOS/iPadOS, use the lock-screen or Control Center media controls. If Android playback stops after the screen locks, see background playback troubleshooting . On Linux Wayland, the automatic Picture-in-Picture trigger for minimizing the window only works on KDE Plasma. On other Wayland desktops, use When the window loses focus or is switched away instead. Desktop window and external-player options do not all apply to the mobile apps.

title: Downloads and offline viewing
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: The download comparison covers FreeTube and OpenTubeX. Downloads need yt-dlp, so they are not available in OpenTubeX Lite or the web demo.

title: Set up downloads
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Settings → Downloads and turn on Enable Downloads if needed. Choose a Download Folder you can write to and that has enough free space. On desktop, leaving it blank saves to your system’s Downloads folder. The Flatpak and the mobile apps need a folder before they can download. On desktop, allow time for any required managed tools to download. OpenTubeX uses yt-dlp and FFmpeg for download tasks; tool options depend on your platform. Downloads settings showing Enable Downloads, Download Folder, concurrent downloads, and bandwidth limit. Select the folder icon in Download Folder to choose where files are saved. The mobile apps use their own storage pickers and download implementations. Grant access to your chosen folder when prompted; desktop executable paths and the choice of system-installed tools do not apply there.

title: Download a video or audio
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Select Download below the video, or Download Video in a video’s menu. In the download dialog, choose the offered format and quality, or an audio-only option when you want sound without video. Confirm the download. Open Downloads from the top bar or profile menu to see progress and queued items. Downloads need a working connection until they finish. Higher-quality video usually uses more storage. Subtitles can be downloaded when offered for the selected video.

title: Reuse settings with templates
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: To reuse a set of download options, select Save Template next to Template in the download dialog and give it a name. Pick it from Template next time. To create or edit templates outside the dialog, open Settings → Downloads → Manage Download Templates .

title: Download new uploads automatically
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: On desktop and Android, Settings → Downloads → Manage Automatic Downloads picks a download template and filters for each subscribed channel. Matching videos download in the background when subscription feeds refresh. Enabling a channel starts with its next upload. OpenTubeX does not download older videos. You can limit automatic downloads to unmetered networks or to while the device is charging.

title: Download from another site
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Downloads and select Add download . If downloads are unavailable, check Settings → Downloads → Enable Downloads . Paste the full media page URL into Video or playlist URL and select Next . Choose the video or audio download options, confirm, and follow progress in Downloads . Add download dialog with a Vimeo media URL entered and a Next button. Paste the media page URL in Downloads → Add download, then select Next. You can also open the link in the player first and select Download below it. Available formats depend on the site and yt-dlp. A supported playback link does not guarantee every download format will work. On iOS, compatible external-site downloads offer Play download inside OpenTubeX. On desktop and Android, open the saved file with a compatible media player. On desktop, use Show in Folder to find it.

title: Play a completed download
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Downloads and find a completed item. Choose Play download to watch the saved media. For downloads from other sites, this is only available on iOS; on desktop and Android, open the file in a compatible media player. On desktop, use Show in Folder to locate the file in your file manager. Keep the file in its saved location if you want OpenTubeX to find it again. Clearing an entry from the list and removing its file are different actions. Remove File moves the file to the trash on desktop and deletes it permanently on Android and iOS.

title: Manage the queue
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Downloads lists queued, running, and finished items. Use Pause all and Resume all for the whole queue, Retry all failed downloads after fixing a problem, and Move earlier or Move later on a queued item to change its order.

title: Download a playlist
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open a playlist’s menu and choose Download Playlist when available. Review the download options before starting: a large playlist can use significant space. The Downloads panel shows the queued work.

title: Manage a failed download
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Downloads and read the item’s error. Check your connection, free space, and access to the download folder. If the error mentions yt-dlp or FFmpeg, check for tool updates under Settings → Advanced → External Software on desktop, or update yt-dlp there on Android. Use Retry download after fixing the cause. If the video itself will not play, start with playback troubleshooting . Include the download error and platform when reporting a bug .

title: SponsorBlock and other add-ons
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: SponsorBlock uses community-contributed segment timings to identify sponsors and other sections inside videos. Coverage depends on contributions: an unmarked segment cannot be skipped automatically.

title: Enable SponsorBlock
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Open Settings → Add-ons . Find SponsorBlock and turn on Enable SponsorBlock . Review each category’s skip option rather than assuming they all behave the same. Open a video with known segments and check the seek bar. SponsorBlock enabled in Add-ons settings with separate Skip Option menus for Sponsor, Unpaid Self Promotion, and Interaction Reminder. Enable SponsorBlock, then choose each category’s Skip Option. Categories can use different behaviors.

title: Choose a skip behavior
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Option What it does Auto Skip Skips segments in that category automatically. Prompt To Skip Offers a choice when a segment is reached. Show In Seek Bar Marks the segment without automatically skipping it. Do Nothing Disables the category’s skipping behavior. Choose different behaviors for categories such as sponsorships and intros. Show notice after a segment is skipped controls the notification; it does not enable or disable skipping itself. To never skip segments for a channel, add its channel ID under Excluded Channels . The ID must match exactly.

title: Review a video’s segments
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: To see the segments found for the current video, select Open SponsorBlock info , the SponsorBlock button below the video or in the player. From this panel you can: Upvote or Downvote a segment, or skip or mute it on demand. Turn Automatically skip segments off for the current video only. Whitelist channel to stop auto-skipping for that channel’s videos.

title: If the wrong part is skipped
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Check which category is responsible. For a one-off, open the player’s SponsorBlock panel and turn off automatic skipping for that video. If the segment’s timing or category is wrong, Downvote it there; votes affect the shared SponsorBlock data. Otherwise, change the category to Prompt To Skip or Show In Seek Bar while investigating. Retry the affected section. If needed, temporarily disable SponsorBlock to compare playback. Segment timing comes from contributors and can be inaccurate. When reporting an OpenTubeX problem, include the public video URL, segment time, category, and chosen behavior.

title: Contributions and identity
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Enable SponsorBlock Submission is separate from enabling playback skipping. Review it if you want to contribute. Turning it on shows Private user ID (optional) , where you can paste the private ID from the SponsorBlock browser extension. Keep that ID private; it is not something to include in a bug report. Leaving it empty lets the app use its generated ID.

title: Other add-ons
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: In Settings → Add-ons , review Use DeArrow Video Titles , Use DeArrow for thumbnails , and Enable Return YouTube Dislike if you want alternative titles, thumbnails, or dislike information. These are optional services and their results may differ from YouTube’s own display. Two more add-ons are there as well: AiSList hides AI slop channels on a community-maintained blocklist from search, trending, and recommendations, and labels videos from channels on its warnlist. It only applies to results loaded with the Local API. Voice-over translation , on desktop and Android, plays a machine-translated voice-over through the unofficial Yandex service when you request it. It is off by default. Enabling an add-on makes requests to its service. The privacy policy’s network exposure table describes what each service can observe. An add-on outage does not necessarily mean the video provider itself is unavailable.

title: Troubleshooting and bug reports
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.

title: A video will not play
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Try a second public video. If only one fails, it may be removed, private, region-restricted, or otherwise unavailable. For age-restricted or members-only videos, see below . Check your connection and restart OpenTubeX. Update the app . YouTube changes can break extraction in older versions. If you changed playback or provider settings, review them under Playback and Advanced . Try returning the affected option to its default and retry the same video. Check existing issues for the same error before opening a report. For buffering, try a lower quality in the player. With the Local API, Always use backup media server in Settings → Advanced can help when YouTube’s assigned server is slow. If you use a proxy or an alternative provider, check whether the problem also happens without that configuration. Note which setting made a difference. If search and channel pages work but videos fail, OpenTubeX already tries the other stream extraction method by default. The error message also offers Retry with built-in extraction or Retry with yt-dlp extraction . Include the failing method in your report. To keep a recovery error on screen instead of a brief notification, turn on Settings → Playback → Pause on Stream Recovery . If the error says YouTube has blocked your IP address, switch to a different VPN or proxy, or try another provider .

title: Age-restricted or members-only videos
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Age-restricted videos need an age-verified Google account. Members-only videos need a Google account with an active membership to the channel. On desktop and Android, configure cookies under Settings → Advanced → yt-dlp Cookies , then choose Try with configured cookies on the video. Using yt-dlp with a Google account can lead to restrictions on that account.

title: Imports or subscriptions look incomplete
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check the active profile and try All Channels . Review feed filters and refresh the subscription feed. For an import, check the success or skipped-item message and confirm that you used a supported format . Keep the original export so you can retry or investigate missing entries. An imported channel list does not instantly contain every video. Refreshing the feed needs a working connection. Do not clear your data as a first troubleshooting step.

title: Repair imported history
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: If imported history entries have missing titles, channels, or publication dates, incorrect durations, or incorrect LIVE labels: Open History and choose Repair History . On narrow screens, the button reads Repair . Review the description, then choose Start repair . Keep a working internet connection and let the repair run. Large histories can take time; failed requests are retried automatically. Check the repaired and failed counts, then review the affected entries. Repair History dialog explaining which details are checked, that watch progress stays unchanged, and the Start repair action. Review what Repair History changes, then select Start repair. Repair fetches video details while preserving watch progress and watched status. Deleted or private videos may remain incomplete. It cannot recover watch events that were absent from your export. Keep the original export while investigating missing data.

title: Downloads fail or saved files are missing
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check the chosen download folder, storage permission, and free space. Moving or deleting a saved file outside OpenTubeX can make its list entry unavailable. On desktop, a download error mentioning external tools may require updating the managed tools. Follow the download troubleshooting steps .

title: Android background playback stops
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Confirm that playback works with the app in the foreground. In OpenTubeX, check that Settings → Playback → Continue playback when the screen is locked is on. Open Android’s app information for OpenTubeX and review its battery/background usage settings. Allow background activity if Android has restricted it; names vary by device. Check notification permission if media controls are missing. Test again with the screen locked and note whether the problem happens on Wi-Fi, mobile data, or both. Include your Android version and device model in a report. Desktop and Android behavior may differ.

title: The app will not open after installation
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check that the package matches your processor and meets the requirements on the Downloads page . Extract portable archives before running them. On Linux, check the executable permission for an AppImage. On macOS, review the first-launch instructions in the installation guide . Before reinstalling or clearing storage, export your data if the app still opens. Clearing application data can remove your local library and settings.

title: Report a bug
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Search the OpenTubeX issue tracker for your error or symptoms. If no existing issue matches, select New issue and use the bug-report template. Include the OpenTubeX version, operating system/version, installation method, and whether you use a regular release or nightly build. For mobile apps, include the device model. Write numbered steps that reproduce the problem, what you expected, and what happened instead. Include the affected video URL if it is public and relevant. Copy the exact error text and attach a screenshot or short recording if it explains the problem. Mention any settings changes or workarounds you tested. For problems that are hard to describe, turn on Settings → Advanced → Diagnostics → Enable diagnostic logging , reproduce the problem, then choose Copy report or Save report and attach it. Diagnostic logs stay in memory until you copy or save them, and turning logging off deletes them. Reports leave out cookies, tokens, IP addresses, and URL parameters, but can include IDs of videos you played. Check a report before you share it. Remove personal information from screenshots and logs. Do not attach cookies, passwords, sync recovery information, or your full viewing database to a public issue. For help using the app, you can also ask in the Matrix community or Fluxer community .

title: Choose a content provider
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: A content provider retrieves video and channel information. It is separate from your local subscription library and from the player that plays the media.

title: Local API and Invidious
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Local API retrieves information directly from YouTube using the extractor included with OpenTubeX. YouTube receives those requests. If a YouTube change breaks extraction, an app update may be needed. Invidious API retrieves information through the Invidious server you select. That server contacts YouTube on your behalf and can observe your requests. Its availability depends on the operator and whether YouTube is blocking it. Neither option requires you to transfer your local subscriptions to a YouTube account. Choosing Invidious alone does not guarantee that every connection avoids YouTube: video proxying, fallback, and other enabled features also matter.

title: Change the provider
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Open Settings → Advanced . Find Preferred API Backend under the provider settings. Choose Local API , Invidious API , or Yattee Server . If choosing Invidious, review Invidious instance and select the server you intend to use. If choosing Yattee Server, enter your server’s details as described in Use your own Yattee server . Retry the same search or video to check the change. Advanced settings showing Preferred API Backend, fallback, stream extraction, and video proxy controls. Preferred API Backend and fallback are in the Video and metadata providers section of Advanced settings. Use settings search if the controls are not immediately visible. Choose an instance you trust rather than pasting an unknown server address solely because it appears in an error workaround.

title: Choose a stream extraction method
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: In Settings → Advanced → Video and metadata providers , find Stream extraction method . This chooses how the app obtains playable streams; Preferred API Backend controls the provider used for video and channel information. A page loading successfully does not necessarily mean its media streams can be extracted. Method When to use it Built-in Use the app’s included stream extraction. Live streams and premieres play at the live edge without seeking. yt-dlp Use yt-dlp for stream extraction, including seeking in live streams and premieres when YouTube provides a rewindable stream. It must be available, and videos may take longer to start. Stream extraction method menu offering Built-in and yt-dlp beside the separate Preferred API Backend control. Stream extraction method selects how to obtain playable streams; Preferred API Backend is a separate choice. The stream extraction method is not available in OpenTubeX Lite or the web demo, which have no yt-dlp. On desktop and Android, configure or update yt-dlp under Settings → Advanced → External Software . On Android, that section offers Update yt-dlp and yt-dlp cookies; desktop executable paths only apply on desktop. Automatically switch stream extraction methods is on by default. If one method fails, OpenTubeX tries the other. To pick a method for a single video, select the Change Media Formats button below the video. If search and channel pages work but playback still fails, note which method you tried, try the other one, and retry the same public video. Record which method worked when reporting the problem. The method does not download a permanent offline copy; use Downloads for that.

title: Understand fallback
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Fallback to Non-Preferred Backend on Failure allows the app to try another backend when the preferred backend fails. It is off by default. Fallback can improve availability, but it can also send requests to a service you were trying to avoid. When an Invidious or Yattee request falls back to YouTube directly, OpenTubeX warns that your IP address is exposed to YouTube. Search settings for fallback , review the setting, and leave it off if you need to control which provider receives requests. Trending needs the Local API; with Invidious or Yattee Server, it only works when fallback is on. Record your original settings before troubleshooting so you can restore them afterward.

title: Proxy video through Invidious
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Search settings for Proxy Videos Through Invidious to review video proxying. It is only available while an Invidious instance is in use. When supported by the selected playback path, this sends video requests through the instance rather than directly to YouTube. Proxying can affect speed and availability. Do not assume this switch controls external players or every playback engine. OpenTubeX’s privacy policy describes exposure for local extraction, Invidious, and yt-dlp separately.

title: When a provider stops working
description: Understand metadata providers, stream extraction, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Try another public video, check for an app update, and check whether the selected instance is reachable. With the Local API, if videos often buffer, try Always use backup media server , which streams from YouTube’s backup server instead of the assigned one. If you change providers as a test, note whether search, channel pages, or playback improved; that distinction helps a bug report .

title: Use your own Yattee server
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Yattee Server is a self-hosted server that loads YouTube data with YouTube’s internal API and yt-dlp. With Yattee Server as the preferred API backend, OpenTubeX sends searches, channel and playlist pages, comments, and video requests to your server instead of to YouTube or a public Invidious instance. The server can also relay the video and audio streams. Thumbnails still load directly from YouTube. Choose a content provider explains how the backend, fallback, and proxying settings work together.

title: Before you start
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: You need a computer that runs Docker and that your devices can reach. Use an HTTPS address if you watch on Android or iOS. Android cannot play videos from a server on http:// . A domain with a reverse proxy works, as does a private network that provides HTTPS certificates, such as Tailscale. The desktop app can also connect to http:// addresses on your local network.

title: Start the server
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Create a docker-compose.yml file with a username and a long password of your choice: services: yattee-server: image: yattee/yattee-server:latest container_name: yattee-server ports: - "8085:8085" environment: ADMIN_USERNAME: alex ADMIN_PASSWORD: replace-with-a-long-password CORS_ORIGINS: https://localhost,capacitor://localhost volumes: - data:/app/data - downloads:/downloads restart: unless-stopped volumes: data: downloads: Start it with docker compose up -d . ADMIN_USERNAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD create an admin account when the server starts. Once an account exists, the server asks for a username and password on every request. You can add accounts for other people in the admin panel. CORS_ORIGINS lets the Android and iOS apps load video streams from the server. The desktop app does not need it. To use the server from the web demo , add https://opentubex.org to the list. To check that the server runs, open http://localhost:8085/admin in a browser on the server computer and sign in. From other devices, use the HTTPS address from the next section, so that the password is not sent unencrypted. The yattee-server configuration reference lists the other options.

title: Add HTTPS
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Put a reverse proxy in front of the server that handles HTTPS and forwards requests to port 8085. The proxy must pass on the original Host header and set X-Forwarded-Proto , because the server builds the stream URLs it returns from them. Caddy does both by default and obtains a certificate for the domain. A Caddyfile for it: yattee.example.com { reverse_proxy localhost:8085 } With nginx, add these lines to the location block of an HTTPS server: proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8085; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; If the reverse proxy runs on the same computer, change the port mapping to "127.0.0.1:8085:8085" so that other devices can only reach the server through HTTPS.

title: Connect OpenTubeX
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Open Settings → Advanced . Under Video and metadata providers , set Preferred API Backend to Yattee Server . Enter the Yattee server URL , such as https://yattee.example.com , and the Username and Password of an account on the server. Choose Test Connection . OpenTubeX reports Connected to Yattee Server and the server’s version. Search for a video and play it. Video and metadata providers settings with Yattee Server selected, the server URL, username and password fields, and a successful connection test. The server address shown is an example. The server URL, username, password, and proxy setting stay on the device. OpenTubeX does not export or sync them, so enter them again on each device. If the connection test fails, it names the problem, such as a wrong password or a missing CORS_ORIGINS entry. Correct it and test again.

title: Proxy videos through the server
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Proxy videos through the Yattee server is on by default. The server then relays the video and audio streams, and the player does not connect to YouTube. Turn it off only if the server uses the same internet connection as your device. YouTube serves a stream only to the IP address that requested it, so playback fails when the server is elsewhere.

title: Limitations
description: Run yattee-server and connect OpenTubeX to it for search, channels, and playback.
text: Yattee servers do not provide community posts, hashtag pages, Trending, or live chat. Comments and channel tabs cannot be sorted, and search feature filters such as HD or subtitles are hidden. With Fallback to Non-Preferred Backend on Failure turned on, OpenTubeX loads posts, hashtag pages, Trending, and live chat with the local API, which connects to YouTube directly. With fallback turned off, these pages show a message instead. yattee-server 1.0.10 and earlier do not relay live streams. With those versions, live streams only play with proxying turned off, and only if the server uses the same internet connection as your device.

title: Privacy and watch history
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: OpenTubeX keeps its library on your device by default. It reduces reliance on the YouTube website, but it does not make network requests anonymous. For details, see the privacy policy .

title: Choose what to remember
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Open Settings → Privacy . Review Remember Watch History and Remember Search History . Choose a Save Watched Progress mode if you want to resume videos where you left off. Auto saves while you watch, Semi-auto saves only when you pause or finish a video and adds a Save Watched Progress button below the player, and Never turns saving off. It is unavailable while watch history is off. For viewing statistics, open Settings → General and review Enable Watch Statistics . Privacy settings showing watch history, search history, and Save Watched Progress controls. Use the history toggles to choose what to remember and Save Watched Progress to control resume behavior. Turning off future recording is different from deleting existing entries. Use the relevant removal action when you also want to clear saved data.

title: Limit history retention
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Storage and find Automatic History Retention (Days) in the watch-history controls. Leave it blank to keep history indefinitely, or enter a positive whole number to retain a limited number of days. Saving a retention period removes older entries immediately and continues applying the limit while the app is open. Export history first if you may want it later.

title: Clear data
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Storage and select Remove Watch History or Delete search history , then read the confirmation. Clearing watch history is not the same as unsubscribing or removing playlists. For storage and cache cleanup, see Data and storage . Avoid clearing every category to troubleshoot a single playback problem.

title: Understand network privacy
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Local extraction and downloads can contact YouTube directly. Playback and downloads from external media links also contact the selected site and its media services. Invidious sends relevant requests to the chosen instance; video proxying and fallback affect which other connections occur. SponsorBlock, DeArrow, and other add-ons contact their respective services when used. With the default public sync server, or another server with enhanced privacy, sync is end-to-end encrypted. The app encrypts the selected data on your device before uploading it. LibreTube sync servers do not support this, and their operators can read synced data; the app warns you when that applies. See Sync between devices for setup and category selection. Internet connectivity checks sends small requests to a GrapheneOS-hosted service to check internet access. Review its toggle in Privacy settings. A receiving service can observe your IP address and request details unless the relevant connection is routed through an intermediary. Profiles are not separate security identities. See Choose a content provider for the provider settings, and the network exposure table for service-specific details.

title: Share a useful bug report privately
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Before attaching a screenshot or log to a public issue, remove cookies, passwords, recovery information, and personal viewing data. Usually a public video URL, exact error, app version, and reproduction steps are more useful than an entire database.

title: Data and storage
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Use data exports to transfer your library between devices. Use the storage view when you need to locate the desktop profile or understand disk usage.

title: Open the desktop profile directory
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage . Select Storage . Choose Open profile directory to open the current profile folder in your file manager. This is more reliable than assuming a fixed path: portable apps, sandboxed packages, and development builds can use different locations. Android and iOS use private application storage and do not offer the same desktop file-manager workflow.

title: Default data locations
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Operating system or package Data directory Windows (Installer) %APPDATA%/OpenTubeX/ Windows (Portable) OpenTubeX-data/ beside the executable macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenTubeX/ Linux ~/.config/OpenTubeX/ , or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/OpenTubeX/ if XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set Linux (Flatpak) ~/.var/app/org.opentubex.OpenTubeX/config/OpenTubeX/ Linux (Snap) ~/snap/opentubex/current/.config/OpenTubeX/ Android /data/user/0/org.opentubex.app/ iOS / iPadOS /var/mobile/Containers/Data/Application/<UUID>/Library/ The Android path shown is for the device’s primary user; other users and work profiles have a different user number in place of 0 . Nightly uses org.opentubex.app.nightly in that path instead, and Lite builds add .lite , as in org.opentubex.app.lite . On iOS and iPadOS, <UUID> is the system-assigned identifier for this installation’s app container. These mobile directories are not accessible through normal file managers. Use data exports to back up or transfer your library.

title: Understand the desktop files
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: File Contents profiles.sqlite Profiles and subscriptions settings.sqlite Application preferences playlists.sqlite Local playlists and saved videos history.sqlite Watch history and saved progress watch-stats.sqlite Watch-time statistics tab-session.sqlite Saved tab sessions search-history.sqlite Saved searches subscription-cache.sqlite Cached subscription-feed entries live-reminders.sqlite Reminders for upcoming live streams and premieres recommendations.sqlite Data for local recommendations video-metadata-cache.sqlite Cached video details downloads.json Download list and records yt-dlp-playback-cache.json Cached yt-dlp stream information Each database can have -wal and -shm files beside it that hold recent changes. Copy them together, and only while OpenTubeX is closed. A profile created by OpenTubeX 0.36.1 or earlier also keeps its earlier .db file for each of these. OpenTubeX imports it once and leaves it unchanged, so an older version can still open it. That older version shows your library as it was when it was imported. On desktop, changes you make there are added back the next time you open the newer version. These are application data files, not downloaded video files. Downloads are saved in your configured Download Folder . The profile folder may contain additional caches, session data, and files used by other features.

title: Back up or move to another device
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: For normal transfers, use the export and import actions . They let you choose what to transfer without copying device-specific settings indiscriminately. The unified ZIP backup includes watch statistics, but individual category exports and the ZIP do not include saved tab sessions. A full desktop profile backup includes their database files along with the rest of the profile; it can also contain credentials and sync keys, so keep the whole backup private. For regular backups without copying files by hand, turn on scheduled backups , which save a ZIP backup to a folder you choose. If you need a full desktop profile backup, close OpenTubeX before copying its profile directory to a private backup location. Copy downloaded media separately. Do not edit or replace live database files while the app is running.

title: Free storage
description: Locate desktop and mobile app data, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Storage and review the categories and their descriptions. Prefer clearing a replaceable cache when you only want to reclaim cached data. Read the confirmation before clearing history or other library records. To remove downloaded media, use the Downloads panel and review whether the action clears its list entry or removes the file. On desktop, removed files go to the trash. Storage tab with a disk-usage chart and separate cards for downloaded media, download history records, and replaceable caches. The Storage tab separates downloaded media, records, and replaceable caches so you can choose what to clear. Cleared caches may need to be fetched again, which uses your connection. A cache is not a backup of your subscriptions, playlists, or history. See Privacy and watch history for retention and deletion controls.
